name: Timpanogos North to South Summit Traverse

legs.route: Northeast ridge from the campground road, class 4 face near the top if the scree ledge is skipped

legs.connect: Follow the crest south over the intervening high bump; it is a short walk along the ridge.

legs.route: Faint trail from the ridge down to the main trail, then up the main trail
legs.connect: Continue south along the ridgeline, then pick up the faint path that joins the main summit trail.

legs.route: Trail to the saddle, then a worn scree slope and class 2 scramble
legs.connect: Walk the easy trail to the saddle below the south summit and scramble up.

how: All four summits of the massif can be strung together from a single trailhead, usually starting with the north peak, which has the least obvious start, and ending at the south summit. The ridge between the tops is mostly trail and class 2 scrambling, with class 3 overall; the base of the north peak is the hard part to find, with some steep scrub before timberline. Some parties tag extra small bumps on the crest, and the same line is done in reverse and as a winter ski traverse.
descent: From the saddle below the south summit, drop a steep slope or snowfield to the lake and follow the maintained trail through the basin back to the main trail and trailhead. In early summer the snowfield may need an axe.
logistics: A loop from one trailhead, about 13 to 14 miles with roughly 6,000 to 6,500 ft of gain. Start early to be off the crest before afternoon storms; the snow-free window is roughly summer and early fall.
notes: Three pages read. The FKT page counts five peaks above 11,000 ft but names only the north and south summits. The blog traverse ran south to north on skis in April, from one canyon to the other, exiting via Cold Fusion couloir. Trailhead named by one page only: Timpooneke.

name: Pfeifferhorn, White Baldy and Red Baldy Loop

legs.route: Red Pine Lake route to the east ridge
Heather and talus above the south side of the ridge
legs.connect: Return along the crest to the low point below White Baldy, drop through a notch to the south side and traverse below the ridge, then climb to the summit.

legs.route: Southeast ridge of White Baldy, then the saddle (optional extension)
legs.connect: Go down White Baldy's southeast ridge, using a ramp on the north side to get around cliffs, cross the saddle and scramble up.

how: Climbers go up Red Pine Lake to the Pfeifferhorn first, then come back along the crest and cross to White Baldy; adding Red Baldy turns it into a loop. The crest has a knife-edge section that needs some thought, and the ridge to White Baldy is slow class 2 with a few class 2 plus or 3 moves on talus. The side trip to Red Baldy over White Baldy's southeast ridge is loose and a little dicey.
descent: For the two-peak version, leave White Baldy on its east side to a saddle, cross talus to the White Pine trail and follow it down. For the three-peak version, descend Red Baldy's north ridge to the old road, now a trail. Do not drop off the north ridge of White Baldy; reports call it steep and loose and some parties have been cliffed out.
logistics: One trailhead in the canyon, loop of about 12 to 13 miles with 4,400 to 5,000 ft of gain. Start early since storms build over the crest; snow lingers on the ridges into early summer.
notes: Two pages read. One describes Pfeifferhorn plus White Baldy (class 3, 12.9 mi, 4,400 ft), the other adds Red Baldy (12 mi, 5,000 ft). Search results also show many logs of the pairing; summitpost pages returned 403. Pfeifferhorn route name per one page: Red Pine Lake route.

name: Mount Nebo Traverse (South, Middle and North Summits)

legs.route: Steep ridge or gully from the south side

legs.connect: Follow the ridge north; the first stretch is a loose gully where the solid rock on the right climbs easier than scree.

legs.route: Ridge north, dropping to the east side onto a class 2 social trail
legs.connect: The ridge gets technical near the top, so drop east and follow the worn trail up.

legs.route: South ridge or the official trail (optional)
legs.connect: Descend from the high point toward the north trailhead; the north peak can be tagged with slight backtracking.

how: The three summits of Nebo are strung along one ridge and are usually done in a single push, either south to north or the reverse. Reports describe hard class 2 with a short class 3 stretch between the middle and south tops, plus loose scree and some exposure. Route-finding on the ridge and on the bench trail is the main added difficulty over the single climb.
descent: From the high point, take the north trail down to the north trailhead. Then either shuttle a car or walk the road and bench trail back, though the bench trail is faint and gets lost in meadows.
logistics: Loop from the south side is roughly 15 miles with about 5,700 ft of gain, but it is often done as a car shuttle. Go early to avoid thunderstorms; water is scarce high on the ridge.
notes: Three pages read. Peak elevations differ by a few feet between pages. Class: one says hard class 2 (listing class 3), another a short class 3 between middle and south (kept the higher). Another report reached the peak by the northeast ridge from Wolf Pass and did out-and-back over the three tops. Trailhead names are not stated in the text.
